tier_reason: Upgraded from C. doc/BENCHMARKS.md gives the environment (Intel Xeon E5-2698 v4 @ 2.20GHz, 80 cores, Linux 5.15, Go 1.24.0), the exact wrk command and the RPS tables against fasthttp. The server code for both sides is public (bench/blazehttp/main.go, bench/fasthttp/main.go; go.mod pins fasthttp v1.69.0), and the header-parse table maps to pkg/header/parser_bench_test.go. Go build flags are not stated, which matches the Go A-tier precedent (rpcx, cmd-stream-go).

corrections.hardware: Intel Xeon E5-2698 v4 @ 2.20GHz, 80 cores, 125 GiB RAM, Linux 5.15.0 (doc/BENCHMARKS.md environment; the README header-parse table is not explicitly tied to it)
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Go 1.24.0 (go.mod and doc/BENCHMARKS.md); go build/test flags not stated; GOGC=100; wrk -t4 -c128 -d10s --latency; h2load -n1000000 -c{N} -m{M}
corrections.claimed_speedup: HTTP/1.1 server vs fasthttp (wrk -t4 -c128 -d10s, doc/BENCHMARKS.md): Plaintext 329,836 vs 298,122 req/s (+10.6%); JSON 328,986 vs 293,992 (+11.9%); POST 1KB echo 313,474 vs 275,830 (+13.6%); p50 latency 179 vs 216 us, but p90/p99 slightly worse (2.99 vs 2.73 ms, 6.41 vs 6.26 ms). Header parsing (README table, pkg/header/parser_bench_test.go): Simple GET (1 header) 252 ns/0 allocs vs fasthttp 1,336 ns/1 alloc = 5.3x; Typical (8 headers) 2,377 vs 6,198 ns = 2.6x; Many headers (20) 4,776 vs 10,077 ns = 2.1x. HTTP/2 vs net/http (h2load): +56.9% to +133.9% req/s.
corrections.caveats: Each wrk/h2load run was done once on a non-isolated system (doc/BENCHMARKS.md), and p90/p99 latency is slightly worse than fasthttp. In the header-parse harness, fasthttp reads through bufio.Reader wrapping a fresh bytes.NewReader on every iteration (the 1 alloc), while BlazeHTTP parses the byte slice directly, so part of the 2-5x micro gap is harness asymmetry. The README does not say which fasthttp variant (reuse or non-reuse) produced the Typical row. The header-parse numbers are not in doc/BENCHMARKS.md, so they are not explicitly tied to the stated CPU. Very low adoption: 2 stars and 18 commits, all 2026-02-21 to 2026-02-24.

notes: All README numbers match. The record's caveat said no benchmark source was public; that is wrong, because pkg/header/parser_bench_test.go, bench/ and doc/BENCHMARKS.md exist. fasthttp is a confirmed catalog entry (wave5 batch-26), so baseline_in_list is now true.

tier_reason: First-party README table: Apple M4 Pro, single thread, gunicorn_h1c ~2.5M / ~4.7M req/s vs httptools ~2.2M and Pure Python ~150K. The repo's only benchmark script (benchmarks/bench_protocol.py) compares gunicorn_h1c's callback API with its pull API. No code reproduces the httptools or Pure Python rows, and no compiler is stated.

corrections.workload: HTTP/1.1 request-parsing loop from Python, requests/sec on Apple M4 Pro (single thread). gunicorn_h1c is a CPython C extension that wraps the vendored picohttpparser. The README says the H1CProtocol row is a Simple GET with a reused parser (209 ns/op); the request type for the other rows is not stated. The comparison is against httptools (llhttp-based) and a 'Pure Python' parser.
corrections.claimed_speedup: gunicorn_h1c (fast): ~2,500,000 req/s; gunicorn_h1c (H1CProtocol, reused): ~4,700,000 req/s; httptools: ~2,200,000 req/s; Pure Python: ~150,000 req/s. That is ~1.14x vs httptools for parse_request_fast and ~2.1x for reused H1CProtocol (derived from page data).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: -O3 (setup.py extra_compile_args; plus -msse4.2 on x86 only); compiler and Python version not stated
corrections.caveats: The README table has no benchmark script for the httptools or Pure Python rows. The only script (benchmarks/bench_protocol.py) compares the callback API with the pull API. The ~4.7M row reuses the parser, and httptools' setup is not described, so like-for-like is unclear. The README claims NEON SIMD on ARM, but the vendored picohttpparser and the module sources contain only an SSE4.2 path. On the Apple M4 Pro used for the numbers, parsing is therefore scalar. httptools wraps llhttp, so this is only an indirect llhttp comparison. Very low adoption: 10 stars.

notes: Numbers match the README. GitHub reports NOASSERTION only because LICENSE appends picohttpparser's MIT notice. The project's own code is MIT, so license=MIT and usability copyable stay. Last commit 2026-08-23, active.

tier_reason: First-party results ('this machine, 3 runs') from public code (benchmarks/cpp/abspath_fix_verification/fair_compare.cpp), directly against unmodified ada::url_aggregator. No CPU, compiler or flags are stated. The urls.txt corpus and the renamed urlparser_old/new sources are not included, so the run is not reproducible as published.

corrections.workload: Single-process, interleaved A/B/C loop, 12 rounds x 4 reps over a urls.txt corpus. Each op parses one URL and reads protocol, host, path (abspath / get_pathname), query and fragment. The three sides are liburlparser OLD (pre-fix), liburlparser NEW (abspath fast-path + cache) and ada::parse<ada::url_aggregator>. This is the parse_url comparison summarized in benchmarks/OPTIMIZATION_NOTES.md.
corrections.claimed_speedup: Full parse + component-extraction ops/s: liburlparser NEW ~7.4-7.8M vs ada ~6.0-6.1M, new vs ada ~1.24-1.29x as stated on the page. OLD was ~5.4-5.5M, old vs ada ~0.90-0.91x. OPTIMIZATION_NOTES.md TL;DR: 'C++ parse_url vs ada: 22.7% behind -> ~1.24-1.29x ahead'.
corrections.caveats: No CPU model, compiler or flags are given ('this machine', 3 runs). The urls.txt corpus and the urlparser_old/new namespace-renamed sources needed to build fair_compare.cpp are not in the repo. ada is a WHATWG-conformant parser with full normalization, and liburlparser is not documented as WHATWG-conformant (its focus is PSL domain splitting). The work per op may therefore differ. The win came from fixing liburlparser's own abspath() cost, not from a faster core parser. License conflict: README says MIT, but LICENSE is pybind11's BSD-3-Clause text with 'The Pybind Development Team' as copyright holder. GitHub reports NOASSERTION. Both candidates are OSI-permissive.

notes: The benchmark_url used /blob/main/ and returns 404, because the default branch is master; it is corrected to /blob/master/. The record's workload was wrong: the benchmark times a full parse plus five accessor calls per URL, not isolated abspath() calls. The numbers match exactly. Metadata checks out: 21 stars, last commit 2026-09-25, not a fork.
